tools.name: dns
tools.description: Use when you need the current DNS records of a domain or hostname: resolves the requested record types live over DNS-over-HTTPS (Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 with Google fallback) and returns every answer with TTL, plus the response code (NOERROR/NXDOMAIN) and whether DNSSEC validated. Up to 8 types per call.

tools.name: rdap
tools.description: Use when you need to know who registered a domain through (registrar), when it was created, when it expires, its EPP status (e.g. clientTransferProhibited), nameservers and DNSSEC: queries the authoritative registry RDAP server (the modern WHOIS) found via the IANA bootstrap. tools.name: availability
tools.description: Use when naming a product, company or project and you need to know which domains are free: checks up to 10 domain names in one call against the authoritative registry RDAP servers (DNS delegation as fallback for TLDs without RDAP) and returns registered / available / likely-available / unknown per n

tools.name: email_security
tools.description: Use when you need to check whether a domain is protected against email spoofing or set up for deliverability: reads MX (and guesses the mail provider), SPF (qualifier, lookup count), DMARC (policy, pct, report addresses), DKIM on common selectors, MTA-STS (record and policy mode), TLS-RPT and BIMI,

tools.name: ssl
tools.description: Use when you need to know whether a website or mail server has a valid HTTPS certificate or when it expires: opens a live TLS connection (SNI) to the host and returns whether the chain is publicly trusted (with the exact error, e.g. CERT_HAS_EXPIRED or self-signed), whether the certificate matches t

tools.name: subdomains
tools.description: Use for attack-surface mapping, asset inventory or competitive research: lists every hostname under a domain that appears in unexpired publicly-logged TLS certificates, deduplicated, with wildcard flag, first-seen date, latest certificate expiry and issuer. Data from crt.sh (Sectigo) with Cert Spott

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: email_security · Private data: dns, email_security · Public sink: email_security.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: email_security · Private data: dns, email_security · Public sink: email_security

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
